title: Your GFlowNet Secretly Learns an Optimal Transport Plan
one_line_en: Fixing the initial edge-flow distribution L in a minimum-flow non-acyclic GFlowNet turns its objective into a Kantorovich OT problem with graph shortest-path ground cost (Theorem 3.2), so the optimal forward policy encodes an executable optimal transport plan rather than a static coupling matrix.
one_line_zh: 在非无环 GFlowNet 的最小总流问题上固定第一步边流 F(s0->u)=L(u)，目标函数就精确变成以图最短路为 ground cost 的 Kantorovich OT（定理 3.2），最优前向策略给出的不是静态耦合矩阵，而是可在隐式组合图上逐步执行的传输路由策略。
key_results: Theorem 3.2: GFlow* = OT* and the induced trajectory distribution yields an optimal coupling Pi*_{u,x} = sum_{tau: u->x} P*(tau)
Theorem 3.3 / Theorem A.5: dual potentials equal BFS distance d(s); complementary slackness F*(s->s')(pi*_{s'} - 1 - pi*_s) = 0 confines optimal flow to the shortest-path subgraph
Appendix A.1 (Prop. A.1/A.2, Cor. A.3): eliminating P_F and P_B turns bilinear detailed balance into a linear program
Appendix A.4: extended dual maps onto Kantorovich dual via a_x = pi_x, b_u = -pi_u with a_x + b_u <= d(u,x)
Table 1 hypergrid: E|tau| matches POT OT* (e.g. H=10 Moon 4.352 vs 4.351) while TV-hat stays at or below the perfect-sampler reference
Table 2 permutations: n=4 E|tau| 0.557 vs OT* 0.567, n=8 1.010 vs 1.008 at lambda=1e-2; n=20 has no tractable OT* reference
assumptions: s0 has no incoming edges, s_f no outgoing edges; s0 exits only into U, s_f entered only from X
every pair (u, x) in U x X connected by a finite path
both marginals normalized: sum_u L(u) = sum_x R(x) = 1, hence Z = 1 is known
unit-length shortest-path ground cost d(u,x) = |tau_{u,x}| (unweighted, possibly asymmetric)
R(x) > 0 for all terminal x (needed for dual optimality in Theorem 3.3)

coupling-level error metrics or measured primal-dual gap
any bound relating balance residual to OT suboptimality
